newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Fox sees huge alien-related revenue.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Fox sees huge alien-related revenue.

text.p: News Corp Ltd's Hollywood studio 20th Century Fox could reap revenues of around US$700 million from its hit film "Independence Day", Peter Chernin, chairman of Fox Filmed Entertainment, said on Friday.

"Right now we are a little bit over US$450-$460 million worldwide box office and that's about $275-$280 million in the U.S. and about $130 million or $140 (million) internationally," Chernin told Reuters on Friday in Sydney.
"I guess we are going somewhere $350 (million), $400 (million) internationallly and to about $300 (million) in the U.S.," Chernin said.

Independence Day, which has invaded cinemas across the United States making it the biggest blockbuster of the summer there, is about an devasting attack on earth from aliens from outer space and how the world.
But Chernin said he was unsure how much the film would contribute to News Corp's bottom line profit.

"There are a lot of variables, because a lot of it has to do with timing. When it comes in, it gets accounted when it comes in so it will fall into this financial year, video will play a large part, there is a lot money in it," Chernin said.

However, Chernin said Independence Day was unlikely to become the biggest grossing film. "I assume in the U.S. we will end up somewhere at number five, we won't beat Jurassic (Park), we won't beat E.T., I don't think we will beat (Forrest) Gump and we won't beat Star Wars," Chernin said.
"I think we are seventh or eighth right now and we are going to number five," he said.
He said the film has only opened in four key international markets so far, Australia, South Korea, Mexico and Britain.
"We haven't opened in Japan, which will be huge, and also in other major markets, Germany, France, Italy and Spain," he said.
Chernin, who is in Sydney to announce a deal with Australian-backed independent flim maker Icon Productions, said the launch of Indpendence Day on Thursday was a huge success.
"Yesterday it looks like we did between US$1.6 million and $1.7 million in just one day in Australia," Chernin said.
He said it beat the previous Australian box office record of $900,000.
Although Chernin was unsure how much profit the film would make, he added: "It's a lot of money -- we are happy about it."
